points.title: Database and DBMS
points.must: A database is an organised collection of related data; a DBMS is the software that creates, manages and controls access to it (e.g. MySQL).

points.title: Relational database
points.must: Data is stored in several linked tables (relations); each table holds data about one entity; tables are linked by keys.

points.title: Flat file vs relational
points.must: A flat file keeps everything in one table, so data is repeated (redundancy) and copies can disagree; a relational database stores each fact once.

points.title: Advantages of a relational database
points.must: At least two: less redundancy, consistency / integrity, easier updates, powerful queries across tables, security, data sharing.

points.title: Functions of a DBMS
points.must: At least two: defines the structure / data dictionary, stores and retrieves data with queries, checks integrity, security / access rights, many users at once (locking), backup and recovery.

points.title: Table, record, field
points.must: Table (relation) = collection of related records; record (tuple, row) = data about one item; field (attribute, column) = one item of data about every record.

points.title: Data types
points.must: Text / string, integer, real / decimal, date / time, Boolean, with an example field for each; phone numbers are stored as text.

points.title: Field size
points.must: A text field has a maximum length, e.g. VARCHAR(30); CHAR(n) has a fixed length; the size should fit the longest real value.

points.title: Index
points.must: An index stores the values of a field in sorted order with pointers to the records, so records are found and sorted faster.

points.title: Disadvantages of an index
points.must: It takes extra storage and makes inserting / updating records slower.

points.title: Primary key
points.must: A field (or fields) whose value uniquely identifies each record; it cannot be empty or repeated (e.g. StudentID).

points.title: Foreign key
points.must: A field that is the primary key of another table and links the two tables; its value can repeat (one student, many loans).

points.title: Composite key
points.must: A primary key made of two or more fields that together are unique, e.g. (StudentID, SubjectID) in Results.

points.title: Candidate and secondary keys
points.must: A candidate key could be the primary key (e.g. StudentID or IIN); a secondary key is indexed for searching (e.g. Surname).

points.title: Referential integrity
points.must: Every foreign-key value must match an existing primary-key value; the DBMS rejects links to records that do not exist.
